336121.title: Conjecture on the structure of the sets of bounded-coefficient $(q;q)_m$ polynomials
336121.root_acceptance: not requested or claimed; root decides
336121.review_depth: Current arXiv v3 (11 Oct 2017; published Proc. AMS 146 (2018)) Section 4, Table 1 and Conjecture 4.1 read; follow-up arXiv:1911.03707 located (abstract-level).
336121.literal_statement:
Let $h$ be a positive integer, and let $S_h$ be the set of all nonnegative integers $m$ such that every coefficient of $(q;q)_m$ lies between $-h$ and $h$, with at least one coefficient having absolute value $h$. For $h>16$, let $i(h)$ denote a positive integer when $S_h$ is nonempty. **The bounded-coefficient set conjecture.** Either $S_h$ is empty or $S_h=\{i(h)\}$ for $h>16$, and

$$
i(h_1)>i(h_2)\quad\text{when }h_1>h_2>16.
$$

Moreover, for $h>5$, there is a positive integer $M(h)$ such that

$$
S_1\cup S_2\cup\dots\cup S_h=\{0,1,2,\dots,M(h)\}.
$$

The conjecture summarizes the observed structure of the sets $S_h$ in the computed data: beyond $h=16$, each set is predicted to contain at most one value, with these values decreasing as $h$ increases, while the cumulative sets are predicted to form an initial interval of nonnegative integers for $h>5$.
336121.source_name: Alexander Berkovich and Ali K. Uncu, “On some polynomials and series of Bloch-Polya Type”, arXiv:1705.07504 (2017).
336121.historical_screen: No exact-ID or source-keyword hits in campaign ledgers or the 516 lane SUMMARY/results files screened (outputs/history-screen.txt); index absence is not global novelty.
336121.finding: Conjecture 4.1 (with the source data) amounts to: M(m) := max|coef of (q;q)_m| is strictly increasing from m = 25 on (for h > 16) and the cumulative sets form intervals for h > 5. Exact big-integer computation of M(m) for every m <= 1253 found M strictly increasing on 25 <= m <= 1253 (ratios M(m+1)/M(m) in [1.12, 1.25]); Table 1 values reproduced. No counterexample; a proof needs explicit-error Sudler/Wright asymptotics for all m plus a finite computation (analytic, Lean-heavy).

336509.title: The length-restricted antipalindrome sum conjecture
336509.root_acceptance: not requested or claimed; root decides
336509.review_depth: Current arXiv v3 (30 Aug 2017) Section 7.2 read; Rajasekaran 2018 Waterloo MMath thesis (UWSpace) read at the antipalindrome passage: still Conjecture 28, NWA did not run to completion.
336509.literal_statement:
An **antipalindrome** is a natural number whose canonical base-$2$ expansion is an antipalindromic word, meaning that the word equals the complement of its reversal. An even integer has an even least significant bit. For an odd integer length $n\geq 9$, consider even integers whose canonical base-$2$ expansions have length $n$.

**The length-restricted antipalindrome sum conjecture.** Every even integer of length $n$, for $n$ odd and $n\geq 9$, is the sum of at most $10$ antipalindromes of length $n-3$.

The conjecture is intended to be proved using nondeterministic pushdown automata, but the authors' computations were incomplete because their program ran out of space. They hoped to establish it as a theorem in a future version; its truth would imply that every even natural number is the sum of at most $13$ antipalindromes.
336509.source_name: Aayush Rajasekaran, Jeffrey Shallit and Tim Smith, “Sums of Palindromes: an Approach via Automata”, arXiv:1706.10206 (2017).

325116.title: Congruence pattern for the function S(a) modulo 3
325116.root_acceptance: not requested or claimed; root decides
325116.review_depth: arXiv v1 (only version) Section 7, eq. (7.11), Corollary 7.2 and Conjecture 7.3 read. Published as Acta Arith. 162 (2014) 51-64 (per [Ho4] in Hou, Acta Arith. 166.3 (2014)); the published text of the 162 paper was NOT read, so retention of Conjecture 7.3 there is unverified.
325116.literal_statement:
Let $S(a)$ be the rational-valued function defined, for each nonnegative integer $a$, by the right-hand side of equation (7.11):

$$
S(a)=\sum_{0\le j\le\frac{a-1}2}\;\sum_{0\le i\le 2j+2\{\frac{a-1}2\}}(-2)^j\binom ai\binom{a+2j+2\{\frac{a-1}2\}-i}{2j+2\{\frac{a-1}2\}-i}
\left[\binom{\lfloor\frac a2\rfloor+j}{2j+2\{\frac{a-1}2\}}+\binom{\lfloor\frac a2\rfloor+\frac 12+j}{2j+2\{\frac{a-1}2\}}\right].
$$

**Congruence-pattern conjecture.** One has

$$
S(a)\equiv \begin{cases} 0\pmod 3&\text{if }a=0\text{ or }3^{2k+1}\le a\le 3^{2k+2}-1\text{ for some integer }k\ge 0,\\ -1\pmod 3&\text{otherwise}. \end{cases}
$$

This pattern strengthens the preceding congruence for $q\equiv 1\pmod 8$, which gives $S(a)\equiv0\pmod p$ on a specified interval. It is motivated by computer experiments, and no proof or resolution is supplied in the source.
325116.source_name: Xiang-dong Hou, “A Class of Permutation Trinomials over Finite Fields”, arXiv:1303.0568 (2013).

Conjecture 7.3 extends Corollary 7.2 (p = 3, q = 3^{2k}). A proof would need a Lucas-type 3-adic analysis of the double sum; not attempted. An a <= 250 run hit the wall cap (logs/houS250.*) and is not claimed.

323730.title: Sum rules for the three singlets in the cyclic model
323730.root_acceptance: not requested or claimed; root decides
323730.review_depth: Abstract/current version (v2, J. Stat. Phys. 150 (2013) 609-657) checked; conjecture body not reproduced; follow-ups located by search only (Hagendorf 2014 arXiv:1405.4726 nineteen-vertex model; Hagendorf-Morin-Duchesne 2016 sum rules via Kuperberg determinants).
323730.literal_statement:
For odd $N=2n+1$, consider the cyclic spin-chain Hamiltonian with parameters $\lambda,\zeta$ and its three translation-invariant zero-energy singlets $\Psi_N^a$, indexed by $a=0,\pm$, with components $\psi_\mu^a$ in spin configurations $\mu$. Let $\nu_1(\mu)$ be the number of spins equal to $1$ in $\mu$. **The cyclic singlet sum-rule conjecture.** With the stated normalisation, the square norm of each singlet factorises into two polynomials in $\zeta,\lambda$ with positive integer coefficients. Along $\lambda=\zeta$,

$$
\lVert\Psi_N^a(\zeta)\rVert^2=3^{-2n}\left(\sum_\mu\zeta^{\nu_1(\mu)}\psi_\mu^a\right)\left(\sum_\mu\zeta^{-\nu_1(\mu)}\psi_\mu^a\right),\qquad a=0,\pm.
$$

For $\Psi_N^0$, along the same line,

$$
\sum_\mu\zeta^{\nu_1(\mu)}\psi_\mu^0=3^{2n}\zeta^{2n+1}\psi_{11\dots1}^0.
$$

The source presents these as open questions supported by exact diagonalisation through $N=7$.
323730.source_name: Christian Hagendorf, “Spin chains with dynamical lattice supersymmetry”, arXiv:1207.0357 (2013).
323730.historical_screen: No exact-ID or source-keyword hits in campaign ledgers or the 516 lane SUMMARY/results files screened (outputs/history-screen.txt); index absence is not global novelty.

372789.title: Győri et al.'s linear Turán conjecture for linear paths in 3-graphs
372789.root_acceptance: not requested or claimed; root decides

372789.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be an $n$-vertex **linear 3-graph**, meaning that any two distinct hyperedges of $G$ intersect in at most one vertex. A **linear path** of length $k$ is the unique acyclic Berge path of length $k$, and therefore has $2k+1$ vertices.

373032.title: Clay's position-matrix eigenvalue conjectures for the single-shelf shuffle
373032.root_acceptance: not requested or claimed; root decides
373032.literal_statement:
Let $n\geq 3$, and let $M$ be the position matrix of a single-shelf shuffle, with

$$
M(i,j)=\frac{1}{2^i}\left(\binom{i-1}{j-1}+\binom{i-1}{n-j}\right),\quad 1\leq i,j\leq n.
$$

For a vector $v\in\mathbb{R}^n$, write $v(k)$ for its $k$th coordinate.

**Clay's position-matrix eigenvalue conjectures.** The following assertions hold:

1. $(1/4,v)$ is an eigenvalue-eigenvector pair of $M$, with multiplicity at least one, where

$$
v(k)=n^2-3nk+\frac{3}{2}k(k+1)-1.
$$

2. The non-zero eigenvalues of $M$ are $2^{-i}$, where $0\leq i\leq n-1$ is an even integer.

These conjectures concern the spectrum of the position matrix arising from the single-shelf shuffling model. The source attributes them to Clay and provides no evidence here that either conjecture has been resolved.

373723.title: The multicolored cycle matching conjecture
373723.root_acceptance: not requested or claimed; root decides
373723.review_depth: Current v2 (25 May 2026) Theorems 6-7, Remark 8, Conjecture 30, Lemma 31 and the special-case argument read.
373723.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a cycle of length $2\ell$ whose edges are colored with $h$ colors. Let $M_0$ and $M_1$ be the perfect matchings consisting of the even and odd edges, respectively, and let $p_M\in\mathbb Z_+^h$ record the number of edges of each color in a matching $M$. Let $k\in\mathbb Z^h$ lie on the segment between $p_{M_0}$ and $p_{M_1}$. **The multicolored cycle matching conjecture.** There is a matching $M$ of size at least $\ell-h+2$ such that

$$
p_M\leq k
$$

component-wise and

$$
\lVert p_M-k\rVert_1\leq h-2.
$$

The paper presents this as a generalization of the corresponding three-color result and as a possible ingredient for extending the approximation guarantee to graphs with a constant number $h\geq4$ of colors. Its resolution is not given in the supplied text.

373723.finding: Since sum(k) = l for k on the segment and p_M <= k, ||p_M - k||_1 = l - |M|, so the conjecture asks for a matching with p_M <= k and |M| >= l - h + 2. Local search (exact DP slack) for h = 4 up to l = 16, h = 5 up to l = 12, h = 6 at l = 12: no violation. A tight h = 4 instance was found and brute-force verified at l = 10 (edge colours [0,1,0,2,0,2,1,2,1,3,0,3,3,3,0,3,1,1,0,1], p_M0 = (6,3,0,1), p_M1 = (0,3,3,4), k = (2,3,2,3) at t = 2/3; max |M| with p_M <= k is 8 = l - h + 2; logs/cl3-10-4-22.log), so the conjectured bound is attained for h = 4. 376053.title: Bang-Jensen, Picasarri-Arrieta, and Yeo's characterization of champions
376053.root_acceptance: not requested or claimed; root decides
376053.review_depth: Abstract of current v2 (12 Oct 2026) read.
376053.literal_statement:
A tournament $H$ is a **champion** if there exists an integer $c_H$ such that every $H$-free tournament has acyclic dichromatic number at most $c_H$. The notation $TT_k$ denotes the transitive tournament on $k$ vertices, and $\Delta(1,1,k)\Rightarrow TT_k$ is interpreted using the tournament constructions defined in the source. **Bang-Jensen, Picasarri-Arrieta, and Yeo's conjecture.** A tournament $H$ is a champion if and only if $H$ is isomorphic to a subtournament of

$$
TT_k \Rightarrow (\Delta(1,1,k) \Rightarrow TT_k)
$$

for some integer $k\geq 1$. Since every champion is a hero but not every hero is a champion, this conjecture seeks a precise characterization of the tournaments whose exclusion gives a bounded acyclic dichromatic number.
376053.source_name: Pierre Aboulker, Pierre Charbit, Samuel Coulomb, Kathryn Nurse and Lucas Picasarri-Arrieta, “Acyclic Dichromatic Number of Tournaments: these are the Champions”, arXiv:2607.14694 (2026).

366608.title: Generalized oriented Hamilton cycle discrepancy conjecture via s-star
366608.root_acceptance: not requested or claimed; root decides
366608.review_depth: Current v2 (11 Feb 2026, split from v1) Sections 1-2 read (Conjectures 1.2, 1.6, Constructions 1.3, 1.7, Theorems 1.4, 1.5, 1.8). Related Chang-Cheng-Wang-Wei-Yan arXiv:2603.18915 found by search (asymptotic version sigma_2/2 - o(n); abstract-level).
366608.literal_statement:
Let $D$ be an oriented graph on $n\ge 3$ vertices. For distinct vertices $u,v$, call them **non-adjacent** if neither directed arc joins them, and define

$$
s^*(D)=\min\{d(u)+d(v)-n:u\ne v\in V(D),\ \{uv,vu\}\cap A(D)=\emptyset\}
$$

when $D$ has a pair of non-adjacent vertices; set $s^*(D)=n-2$ when $D$ is a tournament. For an oriented Hamilton cycle $C$, let $\sigma_{\max}(C)$ be the larger of its numbers of forward and backward arcs. **s-star discrepancy conjecture.** If $s^*(D)\ge 0$, then there is a Hamilton oriented cycle $C$ in $D$ such that

$$
\sigma_{\max}(C)\ge \left\lceil\frac{n+s^*(D)}{2}\right\rceil.
$$

This is stated as another natural generalization of the cited Dirac-type theorem. The source presents it as open and reports supporting results for the related conjectures.
366608.source_name: Jiangdong Ai, Qiwen Guo, Gregory Gutin, Yongxin Lan, Qi Shao, Anders Yeo and Yacong Zhou, “Oriented discrepancy of Hamilton cycles in oriented graphs satisfying Ore-type condition”, arXiv:2501.05968 (2026).

367590.title: The Pell-equation existence conjecture for $(1,1)$-antimagic graph unions
367590.root_acceptance: not requested or claimed; root decides
367590.review_depth: arXiv v1 (only version) Section 4 read (equation (13), the n = 20 and n = 119 discussion, Conjecture 5). Chen-Fu-Wang-Zhou theorem read at abstract level (Optimization Online 2003 preprint page; Taiwanese J. Math. 9 (2005) 629-638); Project Euclid PDF returned an Incapsula challenge and was not retried.
367590.literal_statement:
Let $P_3$ be the path on three vertices. For a graph $H$, a **$(1,1)$-antimagic labeling** is an antimagic labeling whose vertex sums are exactly $1,2,\ldots,|V(H)|$. **Pell-equation existence conjecture.** Let $m$ and $n$ be positive integers satisfying

$$
(2n+1)^2-2(2m+1)^2=-1.
$$

Then there exist a graph $G$ and an integer $c$ such that

$$
|V(G+cP_3)|=n,\qquad |E(G+cP_3)|=m,
$$

and $G+cP_3$ has a $(1,1)$-antimagic labeling. The preceding discussion motivates this as an existence question for graphs with prescribed numbers of vertices and edges satisfying the Pell equation, especially because components isomorphic to $P_3$ are forced in the relevant setting; the supplied text does not state that the conjecture has been resolved.
367590.source_name: Wei-Tian Li and Po-Wen Yang, “Constructing the antimagic labelings for double stars union paths on three vertices”, arXiv:2503.15296 (2025).
367590.historical_screen: No exact-ID or source-keyword hits in campaign ledgers or the 516 lane SUMMARY/results files screened (outputs/history-screen.txt); index absence is not global novelty.
367590.finding: Full resolution by a short bridge. Take G a disjoint union of stars: partition {1,...,m} into blocks S_1..S_t (t = n - m) with block sums exactly m+1, ..., n; each block becomes a star whose leaves carry its elements as edge labels and whose centre has sum m+i. Leaf sums are {1..m}, centre sums {m+1..n}, so the vertex sums are exactly 1..n; there are m edges and n vertices. Blocks have >= 2 elements since every target exceeds m, so no K2 components; P3 components are the blocks of size 2 (c may be any count, including 0). The partition exists by the Chen-Fu-Wang-Zhou theorem (sum condition = Pell equation (13); all targets >= m). Explicit check for n = 20 (blocks {14,1},{13,3},{12,5},{11,7},{10,9},{2,4,6,8}). This is a classical-theorem bridge and is expected to earn zero credit.

367834.title: Starlike rayless-tree characterization conjecture for compact generated ultrametric spaces
367834.root_acceptance: not requested or claimed; root decides
367834.review_depth: Full source read (v1, only arXiv version); published OJAC 20 (2025) DOI 10.61091/ojac20-01 open-access copy read: Conjecture 6.2 retained verbatim. Companion papers 2402.15774, 2502.04228, 2510.01667, 2607.14098 screened (statements/keywords, not every proof body).
367834.literal_statement:
Let $(X,d)$ be an infinite ultrametric space. A labeled ray is a ray equipped with a labeling that generates the indicated ultrametric space. A tree is **starlike** if it has exactly one vertex of degree greater than $2$, and **rayless** if it contains no ray. **Starlike rayless-tree characterization conjecture.** The following statements are equivalent:

1. $(X,d)$ is the completion of a totally bounded proper subset $X_0\subsetneq X$ generated by a labeled ray.
2. There exists a starlike rayless tree $T$ with a labeling $l:V(T)\to\mathbb R^+$ such that $(X,d)$ is a compact ultrametric space generated by $T(l)$.

The claim is presented as a partial generalization of an earlier theorem in the source. No resolution status is supplied.
367834.source_name: Oleksiy Dovgoshey, Omer Cantor and Olga Rovenska, “Compact ultrametric spaces generated by labeled star graphs”, arXiv:2504.02425 (2025).
367834.historical_screen: No exact-ID or source-keyword hits in campaign ledgers or the 516 lane SUMMARY/results files screened (outputs/history-screen.txt); index absence is not global novelty.
367834.finding: Conjecture 6.2 is TRUE. Complete ordinary proof in CASE-367834.md. (i)=>(ii): total boundedness forces ray labels -> 0, the completion adds one point p with d(p,x_n) = max_{k>=n} lambda_k; cutting the ray after each right-to-left record and hanging each finite segment from p (label 0) gives a starlike rayless tree generating X. (ii)=>(i): compactness forces label 0 at the centre and finiteness of {d(c,.) >= eps}; group each leg by strict prefix records and list groups by decreasing height, each written as (y_{s+1},...,y_e,y_s); this ray with the original labels generates X \ {c}, which is dense and totally bounded.
